description: Akshaya Tritiya — Jains celebrate Bhagwan Rishabhanatha's first ahimsa-based food offering (sugarcane juice) after a year of fasting. Breaking of the year-long fast.
The holiest Jain festival — 8 days (Shvetambara) of intensive fasting, prayer, scripture study and self-purification. The apex of the Jain spiritual year.
ratification_note: DISPUTED, not proven wrong. Council ruled 2027-08-28 and 2028-08-16; the engine gives 08-29 and 08-17, and Drik Panchang (Tier 5, commercial -- QA signal only) agrees with the ENGINE for 2028. description: Samvatsari — the Jain day of universal forgiveness. Micchami Dukkadam: may all wrongdoing be forgiven. Jains seek and grant forgiveness from everyone.
ratification_note: Official-source-backed, PENDING COUNCIL RATIFICATION -- not fully settled. description: Digambara Jain equivalent of Paryushana — 10 days of meditation on the ten supreme virtues: forgiveness, humility, honesty, purity, truth, restraint, austerity, renunciation, non-attachment and celibacy
Jain New Year — the day after Diwali marks the beginning of the Jain calendar year, following the Nirvana of Bhagwan Mahavira
Jain Diwali — marks the Nirvana (liberation) of Bhagwan Mahavira in 527 BCE at Pavapuri. Observed with lamp-lighting, fasting and scripture recitation.
Sacred full moon — commemorates the Nirvana of Bhagwan Rishabhanatha (Adinath), the first Tirthankara. A day for fasting and pilgrimage.
Fortnightly Ekadashi vrat — the 11th tithi of both the waxing and waning moon, a day of fasting for Vishnu.
Fortnightly Pradosh vrat to Lord Shiva — the 13th tithi of both pakshas, observed in the twilight hour.
Monthly full moon observance for Satyanarayan Puja, charity, mantra, and family worship according to tradition.
Monthly new moon observance for stillness, ancestor remembrance, charity, and local family practice.
Monthly Shukla Chaturthi observance for Lord Ganesha, distinct from the Krishna-paksha Sankashti Chaturthi vrat.
Monthly Sankashti Chaturthi vrat to Lord Ganesha — the 4th tithi of the waning moon.
Mondays of the Shravan month, observed with Shiva worship and fasting according to family or sampradaya practice.
Tuesdays of Shravan, especially observed by married women in several regional traditions for Gauri worship.
The Ekadashi that cures diseases and grants liberation (Smarta observance)
